sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:7119
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10836 of 2023

Applicant :- Akhilesh Pandey
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjeev Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Prateek Kumar Srivastava,Veerendra Singh
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that he has received instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be disposed of on merit.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Sanjeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Virendra Singh, learned counsel for the informant and Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Complaint Case No. 07 of 2016, under Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Sakaldeeha,
District Chandauli, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and one another on 13.01.2014 by the then Principal of the College and after investigation,

involvement of the applicant and other accused persons was found false and final report was submitted and against the final report the then Principal filed a protest petition on 17.07.2015 and protest petition has been treated by the court concerned as criminal complaint and in the months of March, 2023, i.e. after eight years, applicant and other accused persons have been summoned.

6. He further submitted that in the year 2016 when Principal of the College changed then new Principal lodged a FIR against the applicant and informant i.e. complainant of the present case with regard to the same allegation and during investigation, again final report has been submitted in favour of the applicant but charge sheet was submitted against the informant i.e. complaint of the present case and in the second FIR, lodged by the new Principal, the informant i.e. complainant of the present case was sent to jail.
He further submitted that this fact clearly suggests that applicant is innocent and he was falsely implicated by the then Principal, who was the real accused.

7. He further submitted that apart from present case, applicant is having criminal history of three other cases but in all the three cases, final report has been filed, therefore, considering the entire facts of the case, applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail till conclusion of the trial of the complaint case, in which, applicant was summoned.
8.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant however, opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.

9. However, learned counsel for the informant submitted that applicant challenged the summoning order before this Court but he could not get the order on merit and a direction was given to him to appear before the court concerned and get regular bail but he is not owing the order passed by this Court, therefore, no leniency should be shown in favour of the applicant and, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail filed by the applicant is liable to be dismissed.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, from the record, it reflects that against the summoning order, which was passed against the applicant in the month of March, 2023, applicant preferred an application under Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. before this Court, in which, a direction was given to the applicant to appear before the court concerned and obtain bail in view of the observation made by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Breau of Investigation and another (2022) 10 SCC 51 but in spite of the order passed by this Court, applicant did not appear before the court concerned and applied anticipatory bail but considering the observation made by the Apex Court in the case of Vinod Kumar Sharma and another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another 2021 SCC Online SC 3225, the instant anticipatory bail application cannot be said to be barred.

12. As far as merit of the case is concerned, initially, during investigation, involvement of the applicant was found false and thereafter on the basis of protest petition, filed by the complainant,
applicant was summoned after eight years in the complaint case and in the mean time, another FIR was lodged by the new Principal of the College against the applicant and complainant of the present Akhilesh Pandey vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7710834/
2 case, in which, again involvement of the applicant was found false and final report was submitted in his favour and charge sheet was filed against the complainant of the present case and he was also sent to jail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Further, however, apart from the present case, it appears that applicant was made accused in three cases but in all the three cases, after investigation, final report has been submitted.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

18. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
